_comment: Prompts the app is graded on, with what a kernel can settle about each.
Every expectation here is a measurement, never a matter of taste: a
bounding box, a hole count, a bore diameter, a volume. That is the whole
point - a score you can argue with is not a baseline. Anything about a
part that only a person can judge stays out of this file and goes to a
bbox is [xlen, ylen, zlen] in mm and may hold nulls for axes the prompt
does not fix. holes counts through and blind bores. bore_dia lists the
diameters that must appear, each once. volume_mm3 is checked to
volume_pct, which defaults to 10 - loose on purpose, because it is there
to catch a part built at the wrong scale, not to grade a fillet.
catalogue: true marks a request the standard-parts catalogue should
answer with no model call at all. Those are the cheapest checks in the
file and the ones most likely to regress silently.

cases.prompt: A rectangular block 50mm long, 30mm wide and 20mm tall.
A cylinder 150mm diameter and 50mm long with a 5mm diameter hole through the centre.
A flat plate 100mm by 60mm by 8mm thick with four 6mm holes, one 10mm in from each corner.
A steel plate 80mm square and 12mm thick with a single 8mm hole through the centre.
A tube 40mm outside diameter, 30mm inside diameter and 60mm long.
An L-shaped bracket, 80mm by 60mm, 5mm wall thickness, 40mm wide.
A hexagonal prism 30mm across the flats and 25mm tall.
A round flange 120mm outside diameter, 15mm thick, with a 40mm bore and six 9mm bolt holes on a 90mm pitch circle.
A stepped shaft: 20mm diameter for 40mm long, then 12mm diameter for 30mm long.
A spacer 25mm outside diameter, 10.5mm bore, 8mm long.
A cover plate 150mm by 100mm by 6mm with a 50mm diameter hole in the middle.
An equal angle bar, 50mm by 50mm legs, 6mm thick, 200mm long.
An M10 flat washer.
A 6203 ball bearing.
cases._note: Three bores, not one: the 17mm shaft bore plus the two raceway faces between the rings, which are cylindrical voids and are counted as such.

cases.prompt: An M8x30 socket head cap screw.
A 20 tooth spur gear, module 2.
cases._note: Tip diameter is module x (teeth + 2) = 44 by definition, which is the check worth making. Face width and bore are the router's defaults for an unspecified gear - five modules and 8mm - not the builder's own signature defaults.

cases.prompt: An M12 hex nut.
A 6mm dowel pin 30mm long.
A NEMA 17 motor mounting plate, 6mm thick, with the four mounting holes and a 23mm central clearance hole.
A GT2 timing pulley with 20 teeth and a 5mm bore.
